newsitem.title: FRANCE: MATIF changes white sugar delivery process.
newsitem.headline: MATIF changes white sugar delivery process.

text.p: The French futures exchange MATIF announced two adjustments on Wednesday aimed at improving the delivery process of its white sugar contract.
In a statement MATIF said the changes would apply to the March and May 1998 expiries and onwards.
The two contracts were temporarily closed on December 5 to allow for the adjustments and reopened at 0945 GMT on Wednesday.

The first adjustment consisted of offering the seller of a contract the possibility of physically delivering sugar either in polyjute or polypropylene bags. Until now physical delivery had to be made in polyjute bags.
If polypropylene bags were chosen a packing differential would be paid to the buyer, MATIF said.
MATIF said the change was introduced to "keep the futures market in line with the physical market where a shift from polyjute to polypropylene has been observed in recent years."
The second change involved the obligation for the seller to specify either polyjute or polypropylene bags for delivery and to deliver a minimum net quantity of 2,500 tonnes.
MATIF said this obligation was introduced for reasons of cost effectiveness as buyers on futures market often took delivery of a small number of contracts.
MATIF explained this situation was "not efficient considering the costs entailed by a fob delivery procedure."
